audit.why: His level 6 and Yi's first/second on-hit items are the real spikes and both layers already say so, consistent with the chart flipping at index 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer calls Infinite Duress 'point-and-click' in focus.text, loading, enemyWin, breakdown.mid, breakdown.cooldowns and report[5]. Content spikes[0] calls Blood Hunt 'Primal Howl (W)'.
audit.why: Riot's text: Infinite Duress leaps in a direction and suppresses the FIRST champion he collides with for 1.5 seconds — it is a directional leap, not a targeted lock, so it can be sidestepped and it can be dodged with Alpha Strike's untargetable frames. Telling a player it is point-and-click makes them stop trying to dodge the one ability that decides the lane. Primal Howl is E (also 2.5s of damage reduction before the fear); W is Blood Hunt.
audit.corrected: Every occurrence re-keyed to a directional leap with the 1.5s suppress; Blood Hunt named as W; Primal Howl's damage reduction added to report[5].

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.trading framed the whole lane around out-grinding his heal without naming anti-heal.
audit.why: Eternal Hunger heals him below 50% health and TRIPLES that healing below 25% — exactly the HP band where you are trying to finish him. Jaws of the Beast and Infinite Duress heal on top.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds and the 25% triple written into breakdown.trading.

edits.before: R Infinite Duress — his point-and-click suppress leap. It ignores Alpha Strike (my only escape), locks me in place, and is a guaranteed kill if his jungler collapses. Never fight near a wall or in fog when his R is up, and save Flash to break the suppress window.
edits.after: R Infinite Duress — a directional leap that suppresses the first champion it collides with for 1.5s. It is dodgeable: sidestep the line, or be untargetable inside Alpha Strike as he leaps. Never fight in fog with it up, and hold Flash for the follow-up burst.

edits.before: Warwick wins by abusing levels 1-6 when his Q drain-heal and W move speed let him chase me off the wave and his anti-heal-proof sustain out-grinds my Meditate, then landing point-and-click R to suppress-lock me through Alpha Strike for a free kill (often with his jungler). If he gets me 2+ levels or kills down before my items, his lead holds because I never get to scale.
edits.after: Warwick wins by abusing levels 1-6 when his Q drain-heal and Blood Hunt move speed let him chase me off the wave and his sustain out-grinds my Meditate, then landing Infinite Duress to suppress me for 1.5s and burst me down with his jungler on top. If he gets me 2+ levels or kills down before my items, that lead holds because I never get to scale.

edits.before: Track R Infinite Duress above all — it's his only point-and-click answer to Alpha Strike and the whole reason he can kill me; also count Primal Howl (E) since its fear is what interrupts Meditate.
edits.after: Track R Infinite Duress above all — 110s at rank 1, his one piece of lockdown and the whole reason he can kill me; also count Primal Howl (E) at 15s, since its 1s fear is what interrupts Meditate.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 I stabilize as Wuju Style's bonus true damage and Meditate sustain let me take short, defined trades and heal back his chip — but Primal Howl can fear-interrupt my Meditate, so I only channel when his E is down. Level 6 is his spike, not mine: Infinite Duress is a point-and-click suppress that ignores my Alpha Strike escape and is a free kill if his jungler is nearby. My Highlander at 6 is for dodging ganks and refreshing cooldowns, not for winning a straight duel yet.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 I stabilize as Wuju Style's bonus true damage and Meditate sustain let me take short, defined trades and heal back his chip — but Primal Howl can fear-interrupt my Meditate, so I only channel when his E is down. Level 6 is his spike, not mine: Infinite Duress leaps and suppresses the first champion it collides with for 1.5s, which is a free kill if his jungler is nearby. My Highlander at 6 is for dodging ganks and refreshing cooldowns, not for winning a straight duel yet.

edits.before: He wants long sustained trades where his passive + Q heal grind me down; I want nothing or a short Wuju-true-damage burst then walk. Pre-6 I auto only to deny, not to win; post-items I commit only when his R is on cooldown.
edits.after: He wants long trades where his passive and Q heal grind me down; I want a short Wuju-true-damage burst then walk. Bring Grievous Wounds before any long fight — his passive triples its healing under 25% HP. Post-items I commit only with his R down.

edits.before: His level-6 Infinite Duress suppress locks me out of Alpha Strike entirely and is a guaranteed kill setup with jungle, while my Highlander only helps me dodge, not duel him.
edits.after: His level-6 Infinite Duress leap suppresses me for 1.5s and is a guaranteed kill setup with his jungler, while my Highlander only helps me dodge it, not duel him.

edits.before: His R Infinite Duress is point-and-click and bypasses Alpha Strike's untargetability if it's already cast, but once I'm in Q I'm immune to new targeting — so I dodge his R by blinking as he winds up. His Primal Howl fear interrupts my Meditate channel; his Q and passive heal counter my poke. My Wuju true damage ignores no armor he stacks because he builds bruiser, so it's pure DPS racing.
edits.after: Infinite Duress leaps and suppresses the first champion it collides with for 1.5s, so it can be sidestepped or dodged outright by being untargetable inside Alpha Strike as he leaps. Primal Howl's 1s fear interrupts my Meditate channel, and its 2.5s of damage reduction wastes any burst I dump into it. His Q and passive heal counter chip — Wuju Style's true damage ignores every bruiser resist he stacks.

edits.before: A true EVEN (50.31%) scaling race: Warwick owns the first six levels and one R can decide it, but reach two on-hit items with even farm and Master Yi is the stronger, lane-flipping hyper-carry.
edits.after: A true EVEN (48.14%) scaling race: Warwick owns the first six levels and one R can decide it, but reach two on-hit items with even farm and Master Yi is the stronger, lane-flipping hyper-carry.

edits.before: Warwick out-sustains and out-trades you early: Jaws of the Beast (Q) heals him for a chunk of the damage dealt and his passive lifesteal ramps when you're low, so he wins any prolonged trade. Primal Howl (W) speeds him onto you and Infinite Duress-range senses your low HP — don't let a trade drag out where his healing snowballs.
edits.after: Warwick out-sustains and out-trades you early: Jaws of the Beast (Q) heals him for a chunk of the damage dealt and his passive heals harder the lower HE is, so he wins any prolonged trade. Blood Hunt (W) senses you under 50% health from 4000 units away and speeds him onto you — never let a trade drag out into his healing.

edits.before: Infinite Duress (R) is a point-blank suppress that locks you for the full channel and lets him burst you — as a squishy Yi with no escape, getting ulted usually means dying. Stay above the HP where he'll commit R, and never fight him in his jungle where he can sense and dive you.
edits.after: Infinite Duress (R) leaps and suppresses the first champion it collides with for 1.5s, and that is long enough to kill a squishy Yi outright. It is a line, not a lock-on: sidestep it, or sit in Alpha Strike's untargetable frames as he leaps. Stay above 50% so Blood Hunt never lights you up.
